This example is for the IVR7 (Icepack Vehicle Router 7) model. IVR7 is an advanced vehicle routing problem solver that is easily customisable to most use cases like pickup and dropoff, multi-depot, multiple time windows and fleet mix problems.

The example illustrates the usage of the data upload API as well as model versioning. It builds a simple pickup/dropoff (similar to the basic model). It uses the parent solve-request container for evaluate requests against a versioned model. This is a quicker manner in which to run evaluate requests against the API where a large chunk of model content is required to define the model. The model is sent once and requests are then just run against that model and we handle moving the data around on our side.


### Data 

```{r}

data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')

number_pubs <- nrow(data)

```

The data used in this example is a list of `r number_pubs` pubs in Dublin, Ireland with their associated X and Y coordinates and quantities (amount added to a vehicle at each location).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

if(!("pacman" %in% rownames(installed.packages()))){
  install.packages("pacman")
}

library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse)
p_load(DT)
p_load(dplyr)
```

```{r}
data <- data %>% select(-c(pickupTime,dropoffTime)) %>% mutate(across(2:3, ~ format(round(.x, digits=5), nsmall = 5))) 

datatable(data, colnames = c("Pub Name (id)",
                           "X-Coordinate (X)",
                           "Y-Coordinate (Y)",
                           "Quantity (quantity)")
                           , options = list(dom = 't', scrollY = "200px", pageLength=nrow(data), columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-right', targets = 2:4))))

```

### Running the example

An R script with all the lines needed to run the example can be found [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/examples/blob/master/R/ivr7-4-advanced.R).

The example uses the **iceR** package which will first need to be installed (see information [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/iceR)) and then loaded. Helper functions are also provided in a separate file and need to be read in.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(iceR)

source('ivr7-model-helper.R')

```


Execute the example as follows:

1. **Create an apiHelper object with the model type you'd like to solve**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'ivr7-kt461v8eoaif', configFile = '../config.json')
```


2. **Create the model, add some data to it and upload it**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Create the model
sr <- new (IVR7.SolveRequest)
model <- new (IVR7.Model)

# Load the data
data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')

# Configure the model and add the data to it (See ivr7-model-helper.R for details around some of the methods used below)
model$dimensions <- make_distance_time_cap_dims()
model$locations <- make_locations(data)
model$jobs <- make_job_time_cap(data, src = rep(1, nrow(data) - 1), dest = 2:nrow(data))
model$vehicleCostClasses <- make_vcc_simple('vcc1', 1000, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 1, 3)
model$vehicleClasses <- make_vc_simple('vc1', 1, 1, 1, 1)
model$vehicles <- lapply(1:4, function(i){
  make_vehicle_cap( paste0("vehicle_", i), 'vc1', 'vcc1',
                    2000, # the vehicle capacity
                    data$id[1], # start location
                    data$id[1], # end location
                    7*60,  # 7 AM
                    18*60) # 6 PM
})

# Upload/submit the model via the data upload API (this API allows us to push just the data without anything else)
# NOTE: The data upload service will need to be enabled on your key
data_api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'ivrdata-o43e0dvs78zq', configFile = '../config.json')
data_model <- new (IVRData.CachedModel)
data_model$model <- model$serialize(NULL) # we just saved our model as a byte stream into this data payload
modelID <-  data_api %>% postSolveRequest(data_model)
# If you get an error at this point, just enable the ivr-data services on the client-portal.
# The modelID is now a guid reference to the model we can reference in a solve request.
rm(model) # We can delete the model at this point becasue we've already uploaded it to the cloud

# Tell the solve request to use the model we uploaded
sr$modelID <- modelID

# Set the other relevant information
sr$solveType <- 0 # 0 for optimise, 1 for evaluate, 2 for reoptimise

sr$toString() %>% cat # Basically no information at all, just the model guid

```

3. **Submit the model to the API**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(sr)  
```


4. **Retrieve the model response**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
resp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)
```


5. **Visualise the result**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Tabulate the data in native-R format
tab <- resp %>% tabulate(sr)
tab$nodes %>% head # just inspect the head of the output
tab$edges %>% head # just inspect the head of the output

```
 


### Manipulating the model and evaluating

Since we have a model that is versioned separately from the solve request, we can use the solve request with the task sequence and have that apply to a model.

At this stage we will extract the task sequence from the solved model.


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# In the intermediate example we used the model$taskSequence. 
# We're going to use sr$routes here (because it's outside the $model)

sr$routes <- list() 

vs <- tab$nodes$vehicleId %>% unique() # the unique set of vehicles in the solution
for(v in vs){
  ts <- new (IVR7.TaskSequence)
  ts$vehicleId <- v
  ts$taskId <-  tab$nodes %>%
    filter(grepl(x = taskId, pattern = 'pickup_') |
             grepl(x = taskId, pattern = 'dropoff_'), # you can use whatever convention you want for pickups/dropoffs
           vehicleId == v) %>%
    select(taskId) %>% unlist %>% as.character()
  sr$routes[[length(sr$routes) + 1]] <- ts
}

# Set the other relevant information (in this case, tell the solver to use the evaluation solve process)
sr$solveType <- 1 # 0 for optimise, 1 for evaluate, 2 for reoptimise

sr$toString() %>% cat # now contains the model guid along with the task sequence for each vehicle

# Submit the model to the API
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(sr)          

# Retrieve the model response
evalresp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)  
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Visualise the result
tabeval <- evalresp %>% tabulate(sr)

if(nrow(tabeval$nodes) != nrow(tab$nodes)){  
  stop("whoa, something isn't right in the world...") 
}

```

This examples shows that if you want to evaluate several permutations (i.e. modifications on a UI) then you don't have to resend the model each time. You can send it only when the master data is modified (i.e. times, locations, tasks etc) and then just use an evaluate solve request against a particular task sequence.
